item.description:

King’s Lynn veterans charity seeks new gardening volunteer
A King’s Lynn veterans charity is searching for a new volunteer to maintain its garden following the retirement of Allan Livingstone. Mr Livingstone, who stepped down after two years of service at The Bridge for Heroes on South Clough Lane, was praised for transforming the outdoor area into a peaceful space for visitors and staff.
The charity highlighted the significant contributions made by Mr Livingstone and his wife, Nancy, who both donated their time and personal funds to develop the site. The Bridge for Heroes is now inviting members of the public to apply for the vacant gardening role. Anyone interested in supporting the charity is encouraged to call 01553 760230 for more information.

item.title: North Lynn man fined for shoplifting at King’s Lynn Primark
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn man fined for shoplifting at King’s Lynn Primark
A 32-year-old man from North Lynn has pleaded guilty to theft after stealing a pair of trainers from a store in King’s Lynn. Olegs Belokurovs, of Walpole Road, appeared at the town’s magistrates' court on Thursday.
The court heard that on July 21, Belokurovs entered the High Street Primark, put on an £18 pair of trainers, and left the premises without paying. The defendant, who represented himself, admitted to the offence. Magistrates handed him a £320 fine, alongside a £128 victim surcharge and £85 in court costs. He has also been ordered to pay £18 in compensation to the retailer.

item.title: Further delay announced for Queen Elizabeth Hospital rebuild
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Further delay announced for Queen Elizabeth Hospital rebuild
The completion date for the new Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been pushed back to 2033. Professor Lesley Dwyer, CEO of the Norfolk and Waveney Hospital Group, confirmed the new timeline at the hospital’s annual meeting, though she expects the facility to be fully operational by 2035.
During the meeting, the trust did not rule out changes to the current A&E department. While Professor Dwyer guaranteed that 24-hour emergency care will remain available, she noted that different models of service are being explored. Local councillor Rob Colwell has expressed disappointment regarding the delay, as a community petition to protect vital services at the hospital has now reached 9,000 signatures.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/qeh-rebuild-pushed-back-again-while-axing-of-a-e-not-ruled-9483372/

The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn is set to be renamed the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital. This change reflects a greater focus on clinical research and medical training.
While the hospital works towards this new status, it is currently addressing concerns regarding student placements. Both the University of East Anglia and the University of Cambridge withdrew medical students from the site earlier this year following negative feedback. Hospital leadership is now working to improve the experience for students, with the aim of resuming placements once these improvements are complete.

King’s Lynn man to be sentenced for stalking and death threats
A 64-year-old man from King’s Lynn is due to be sentenced this Monday after being convicted of stalking and making threats to kill. Stephen Smith, of Windmill Court in Fairstead, was found guilty at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court on July 23.
The court heard that between August 2025 and March of this year, Smith sent distressing letters to his victim, posted about her on social media, and waited outside her place of work. He was also convicted of sharing an intimate photograph of the woman without her consent. The case was adjourned for a pre-sentence report to assess the possibility of a custodial sentence.
